symptom: The existing hard-link publisher has a two-name readback-denial window. A Linux-only synthetic renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) candidate published complete staged JSON with a single link and refused existing regular-file and symlink destinations; a post-rename SIGKILL retained strict readback. This is not a production writer or power-loss proof.
lesson: On a supported Linux filesystem, native RENAME_NOREPLACE can combine a single namespace move with collision refusal. Unlike linkSync followed by unlinkSync, a successful rename does not expose the same staged inode under two names during the post-publication window; synthetic post-rename process termination leaves a single-link destination.
guardrail: Treat renameat2 as a Linux-only research candidate, not a drop-in Node or production replacement. Require a reviewed native binding, same-filesystem staging, fail-closed capability detection, EEXIST collision handling, directory-fd identity protection, safe failed-stage lifecycle, independent two-writer/reader tests, file and directory fsync, and power-loss durability evidence. Never weaken strict readback, auto-delete unverified paths, or infer BUY/production authority.
